text:
alice_support: FYI, customer NeonHealth (Private deployment in eu-west) is hitting intermittent API TLS failures + 502s to the private endpoint. They say it started after a config change on their edge firewall. Posting logs and repro steps.
alice_support: Symptoms: client sees TLS handshake failure / certificate verify errors, server logs show 502 Upstream read timeout and occasional 495 TLS error. customer also reports transient 401 when retrying.
alice_support: Repro steps (from customer network):
```
# simple curl that fails intermittently
curl -v https://private-api.neonhealth.internal/health -o /dev/null
* Connected to private-api.neonhealth.internal (10.52.34.10) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection to 10.52.34.10:443
* TLS: handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.52.34.10:443
```

alice_support: They ran openssl s_client -status to check OCSP:
```
openssl s_client -connect private-api.neonhealth.internal:443 -status
---
OCSP response: no response sent
---
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```

alice_support: Packet capture from customer edge shows outbound TCP to ocsp.example-ca.com gets RSTs and never completes. Their firewall team says they only allow a small egress allowlist and recently tightened rules to only known domains; maybe OCSP responders weren't included.

tariq_netops: can you paste a pcap snippet? also which Direct Connect/private VIF are they on? need to check route maps & NAT.

alice_support: attaching pcap excerpt (hexdump):
```
10:12:03.123 IP 192.0.2.45.54012 > 198.51.100.23.80: Flags [S], seq 123456, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
10:12:03.124 IP 198.51.100.23.80 > 192.0.2.45.54012: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, length 0
```

alice_support: customer edge is 192.0.2.45 (on-prem), OCSP responder IP 198.51.100.23 (third-party CA), everything inside the VPC and VIF looks normal per them.

jordan_sre: quick checklist:
- confirm VIF BGP is up and routes to customer prefix present
- check our private endpoint security group / NACLs (unlikely since connection established sometimes)
- check if our egress proxies are doing any TLS intercept / OCSP stapling changes
- check load balancer logs for TLS diagnostic flags

rene_eng: I pulled the LB logs for the timeframe. We see TLS handshake entries with "no ocsp response" and some upstream 502s when backend connection timed out after TLS fail. LB is configured to request stapled OCSP from backend cert chain if present.

deploy-bot: [alert] dx-vif-eu-west-3: flapping detected (3 state changes in 15m) — might be noise but flagging.

tariq_netops: alice, ask customer to allow outbound TCP/443 to the OCSP responder FQDNs and to common CA CRL/OCSP endpoints (examples: ocsp.example-ca.com, ocsp.int.example, crl.example-ca.com) and retest. Also need a pcap from our side (vpc endpoint) to see if packets are leaving their VIF.

alice_support: customer allowed ocsp.example-ca.com for 15 minutes and retried — TLS connections stabilized, no 502s for ~10 minutes. They report degraded but functional. They will add permanent egress rules.

alice_support: temporary mitigation worked. Next steps:
- tariq to pull VIF-level packet capture on our edge to confirm OCSP queries made by client forwarded correctly
- rene to add clearer docs about required CA/OCSP endpoints for Private deployments and include in onboarding checklist
- jordan to confirm load balancer behavior around stapled OCSP and ensure we don't escalate 502 on missing stapled response

tariq_netops: grabbing captures now. early result: we see incoming TCP SYN from 10.52.34.10 -> 198.51.100.23 on port 80/443 getting RST back at our edge (so the block appears on customer side or their downstream provider). will correlate with VIF metrics.

jordan_sre: for postmortem, we should document: customer firewall tightened egress allowlist -> blocked OCSP -> TLS verify fails -> intermittent 502/495 at LB -> app errors. Also note VIF flapping may have exacerbated timing.

rene_eng: I'll draft a short KB: "Private deployments: required outbound endpoints for certificate validation" and include sample ip lists + FQDNs + recommended healthcheck rules.

alice_support: customer will keep opens for OCSP endpoints and we'll keep monitoring. marking as high-priority until KB published. Thanks all :thumbsup:
